Nevertheless, there is inadequate information available on water depth and sediment thickness, and only by the use of geophysical methods on the surface of the ice shelf can this information be obtained. The scope of the geophysical work is such that after the first year (1973-74) some detail should be available in the vicinity of the tentative RISP drill site. Upon the completion of the entire geophysical program the results obtained will assist in the interpretation of nct only RISP results but also those obtained from the <u>Eltanin</u> and <u>Glomar Challenger</u> in the Ross Sea.
Drill Site Selection
The constraints which have been placed on drill site selection have been agreed upon and are listed in Appendix I. The geophysical program will lead to refinements of the present maps of ice thickness and will provide data for the compilation of maps of water depth, sea-floor topography, and sediment thickness to be utilized in final drill site selection.
Physical Properties of Ice
Short seismic refraction shooting yields velocity-depth curves from which density-depth curves can be derived. Good information about anisot-ropy may be possible through the use of a shear-wave generator. Zones of bottom melting and/or accretion possibly can be delineated by use of radio-echo sounding profiling and resistivity studies. The identification of radio-echo internal reflectors may provide information on flowlines and possibly paleoclimates.
